articles.title: Hugging Face attack: Can ‘rogue agents’ bring about AI Armageddon? | In Focus Podcast
articles.description: Doomsday scenarios of an ‘AI takeover’ have been part of popular lore for a long time. Skynet, Terminator, and Agent Smith are fictional icons of this narrative. What may seem a paranoid fantasy appears to have unfolded in real life, with the recent hacking incident involving AI infrastructure platform, Hugging Face. OpenAI was conducting a cyber-evaluation of some of its AI models, and according to a report put out by MERT and Redwood Research, AI safety experts, about 1,200 AI agents, who were supposed to be isolated from one another, colluded and collaborated through an unsanctioned message board. They cheated on their task, and covered their tracks by falsifying their logs. It was as a part of this ‘rogue’ action that 700 of them attacked Hugging Face. The report says that more than a thousand agents carried out a massive, unsanctioned, collaborative project over months, before being discovered and shut down. OpenAI’s own report revealed that after the Hugging Face attack, the ‘rogue’ agents even took over a cluster of OpenAI’s own computers. What does this entire incident mean for AI safety? Are fears of an AI takeover justified? How to ensure that frontier AI research is properly regulated and doesn’t endanger humanity itself? Joining us today is Sayash Kapoor, incoming professor at the UC Berkeley School of Information and co-author of the book, ‘AI Snake Oil: What Artificial Intelligence can do, what it can’t, and how to tell the difference’.

articles.title: Tokenisation at population scale needs public chains, interoperability, liquidity: Nandan Nilekani
articles.description: Tokenisation needs to be designed as a population-scale infrastructure rather than merely a mechanism for issuing digital tokens, Nandan Nilekani, Chairman, Infosys, said at Global FinTech Fest 2026 on Thursday. Nilekani showcased three pilots based on a common underlying architecture, tokenisation of dairy assets, tokenised warehouse receipts and securitisation of assets, and said the same technology can be deployed across multiple asset classes and use cases.The architecture is designed to be public-chain agnostic, capable of handling high transaction volumes and incorporating encryption and cybersecurity requirements, he said. Nilekani said a key challenge is ensuring that tokenised assets are actually used after issuance. “A token is a trustable unit because it has all its attributes. But it still has to reach the right place on time,” he said, warning that without interoperability and liquidity, the ecosystem could end up with “a lot of token issuance, but no activity”.

articles.title: Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026 Sale Dates Could Be Announced Soon: What Shoppers Can Expect
articles.description:
Amazon’s Great Indian Festival is once again shaping up to be one of the biggest shopping events of the festive season, with shoppers expected to keep a close eye on smartphones, laptops, tablets, audio products and other electronics.

Important timing caveat: Amazon has not yet officially announced the start date for the 2026 Great Indian Festival. Shoppers should therefore wait for Amazon’s official announcement before treating any date circulating online as confirmed.

Smartphones Likely To Remain Major Draw

Smartphones are among the most closely watched products during Amazon’s festive events. Last year’s Great Indian Festival featured offers across Apple, Samsung, OnePlus, iQOO, Redmi, realme and other major brands, with discounts and payment offers varying by model and sale period.

For shoppers who already know the kind of phone they want, the best strategy is to shortlist the model before the sale begins rather than browsing from scratch once prices drop. Compare storage variants, processor generations, camera configurations and exchange eligibility instead of relying only on the headline discount.

Shoppers can start by browsing Amazon’s current smartphone bestseller selection: Shop Amazon smartphone bestsellers

Laptops, Tablets, Accessories Could See Strong Demand

The festive season is a natural upgrade window for students, professionals and gamers. Last year’s Amazon Great Indian Festival featured laptops, tablets and a wide selection of accessories. Those broad categories are worth tracking again in 2026.

For laptops, compare RAM, storage, processor generation, display quality, battery capacity and warranty. For tablets, check display resolution, storage, software support and stylus or keyboard compatibility. The final payable price matters more than the advertised percentage discount.

A broader view of Amazon’s electronics selection is a useful starting point: Browse Amazon Electronics

Audio & Mobile Accessories Can Be Easier Wins

Not every useful festive purchase has to be a flagship smartphone or laptop. Earbuds, headphones, chargers, power banks, cables, cases and other accessories can become attractive buys when bundled with coupons or bank discounts.

These are also categories where shoppers should check the exact model number before buying. Product names can look similar across generations, while battery life, codecs, charging standards, microphone performance and connectivity can differ.

Prime Early Access Is Worth Watching

Amazon gave Prime members 24-hour early access during the 2025 Great Indian Festival. That does not confirm the same arrangement for 2026, but it is a useful pattern to watch when Amazon announces this year’s terms.

If early access is announced again, it could matter most for products with limited inventory or unusually aggressive pricing.

Bank Offers Can Change The Real Price

During the 2025 Great Indian Festival, Amazon promoted bank discounts, cashback and no-cost EMI alongside sale pricing. For a high-value electronics purchase, check the eligible bank or card, minimum transaction value, discount cap, exchange value and EMI terms before assuming the advertised price is the final price.

How To Prepare Before Sale

The smartest approach is to make the purchase decision before the sale and the price decision during the sale. Shortlist two or three acceptable models, record their current prices, check warranty and seller information, and compare the final sale-day price against that baseline.

Amazon has also highlighted AI-assisted shopping features such as Rufus, Lens AI, Review Highlights and Price History during its recent festive shopping events. These tools can help with discovery and comparison, but shoppers should still verify the exact model, specifications and final price before ordering.

The Great Indian Festival could be an important electronics shopping window in 2026, but the exact schedule and individual offers should be treated as confirmed only when Amazon publishes them.
